newsitem.title: USA: Conn Gov vetoes study for U-Conn stadium - paper.
newsitem.headline: Conn Gov vetoes study for U-Conn stadium - paper.

text.p: Connecticut Gov. John Rowland vetoed a bill authorizing a study for a new football stadium for the University of Connecticut and creating 57 task forces for other issues, the Hartford Courant reported Wednesday.
Rowland said he rejected the overall bill for technical reasons and because it would prevent him from appointing any members to the task forces, according to the paper.

House Speaker Thomas Ritter, a Democrat and the legislature's leading proponent of a new stadium for the college in downtown Hartford, said the bill will be changed during a special session July 21 and then sent back to Rowland.

Rowland's spokesman, Dean Pagani, said the governor's position on upgrading the UConn football team and building a new stadium--which could cost as much as $100 million--remains unchanged, the paper said.

UConn's board of trustees has approved the move to the Division 1-A level, but the university has been waiting for the state to approve funding for a new stadium to meet division standards. UConn must decide by Dec 31 whether to accept an invitation to join the Big East football conference.
